title: Move
intro: In Normal mode h j k l move the cursor: left, down, up, right. A number before a motion repeats it. These levels are about reaching the target.

levels.title: Right
levels.brief: Move the cursor onto the d. l moves right. Tip: a count repeats a motion, so 3l moves three characters.
levels.hint: Three presses of l also work, but cost three keystrokes.

levels.title: Down
levels.brief: Move to the last line. j moves down.

levels.title: Corner
levels.brief: Reach the X. Two lines down and five to the right.
levels.hint: Order does not matter: 5l2j is the same cost.

levels.title: Back home
levels.brief: Move to the first column. 0 (zero) jumps to the start of the line in one keystroke.
levels.hint: Ten presses of h is ten keystrokes. 0 is one.

levels.title: To the end
levels.brief: Move to the last character. $ jumps to the end of the line.
levels.hint: Think of $ as the end of a line in a regular expression.

levels.title: Up and left
levels.brief: Reach the p of alpha. k moves up, h moves left. Use counts.
levels.hint: Count the characters before you press.

levels.title: Remember the column
levels.brief: Press j once. The cursor cannot sit past the end of a short line, so it clamps. Move down to the d.
levels.hint: Vim remembers the column you wanted, and returns to it when a longer line comes.
